chunks: From him, from Hammad, from al-Mukhtār, who said:

Abū Ḥanīfah entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and he (the Imam) said to him, 'What do you say about a house that collapsed upon a group of people, leaving two boys, one free and the other a slave to his master, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' He said, 'Abū Ḥanīfah said: Half of this one is freed and half of this one is freed.' Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said, 'Not so, but a lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls upon is the free one, and this one (the other boy) is freed, so he becomes a patron/mawla to this one.'

key_terms.أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: Abū Ḥanīfah, the prominent Sunni jurist
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How is the status of two indistinguishable boys (one free, one slave) determined after a disaster according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the jurisprudential dialogue between the Sunni founder Abū Ḥanīfah and Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) regarding the emancipation of two indistinguishable boys (one free, one slave) after a collapse. While Abū Ḥanīfah proposed splitting the status of each boy, the Imam prescribed casting lots (qurʿah) to determine which is free, with the other being freed to become his patron (mawlā). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on qurʿah as a mechanism for resolving uncertainty in inheritance and manumission, contrasting with the Hanafi approach of partial emancipation.
